key_insight: Cherry tomato detachment is most reliable when a compliant fingertip gripper combines measured gripping force with a controlled wrist twist, rather than relying on pulling alone.
engineering_relevance: The paper translates human picking force signatures into a bio-inspired gripper design that balances detachment success with fruit-skin safety for greenhouse robotics.
method: Captured six-axis force/torque data from 150 manual picking trials for gripping, twisting, and lateral pulling.
Used the measured force/torque signatures to design a dual-stiffness Finray fingertip gripper with TPU contact regions and a rigid PLA body.
Validated the hybrid grip-twist-pull strategy on a UR5-Husky platform in simulation and 50 greenhouse trials.
evidence_signal: The autonomous system achieved 86.0% picking success, 2.3% fruit damage, and 8.4 s per fruit, outperforming several alternative end-effectors.
watch_item: Results were demonstrated for one greenhouse setup and cultivar, so performance may vary with fruit size, cluster density, and field conditions.
paper_title: Force Sensor-Based Picking Pattern Analysis and Two-Jaw Gripper Design for Cherry Tomato Robotic Harvesting in Greenhouse
